slide_text: New team member onboarding: what we build, how it fits together, and your first two weeks
speaker_notes: Welcome the new team member. This deck takes about 15 minutes and covers the product, the architecture, and the onboarding plan.

slide_text:
What we build
Atlas is the order management platform behind our online store. It takes orders from web and mobile, charges payments, reserves stock, and keeps customers updated.
Who uses it
Shoppers through the storefront and app, and our support and warehouse teams through the admin console.
speaker_notes: Give the one-sentence pitch, then the key numbers. Mention that the uptime target drives a lot of our design choices.

Read left to right. All client traffic enters through the API gateway. The four services in teal are the code our team owns. Services talk to each other asynchronously through Kafka wherever possible.

slide_text: How an order flows through the system
Shopper submits the cart from web or mobile
Token is validated and the request is routed
Order is written to PostgreSQL as pending
Stripe charges the card; order is confirmed
OrderPlaced event is published to Kafka
Then, asynchronously: the Inventory service reserves stock and the Notification service emails the receipt, both reacting to the Kafka event.
speaker_notes: This is the most important flow in the system. Steps 1 to 4 are synchronous; the customer waits for them. Everything after the Kafka event happens in the background, which keeps checkout fast.

slide_text: Dev, staging and production run on Kubernetes in AWS, defined in Terraform.
Metrics and traces in Datadog, errors in Sentry. Every service has a dashboard.
Argo CD deploys from Git, so reverting a commit rolls production back.
speaker_notes: Every merge to main deploys to staging automatically. Production deploys need one approval. Show them the Argo CD and Datadog dashboards after this slide.

slide_text: Node.js and Go services, REST and gRPC
speaker_notes: No need to know all of these on day one. Focus first on the backend and data rows, since those are where most tickets land.

slide_text: Laptop, accounts and access. Meet your onboarding buddy.
Run Atlas locally. Read the architecture docs and service READMEs.
Pick up a starter ticket and ship your first pull request.
Join the on-call shadow rotation and present a small demo.
Goal by end of week 2: you can explain the order flow and have shipped code to production.
speaker_notes: Set expectations: nobody expects big output in the first two weeks. The aim is a working setup, one shipped change, and understanding the main flow.

slide_text: Who to ask and where to look
Anything at all, especially early on
speaker_notes: Close by sharing the actual links and introducing the buddy in person. Invite questions.
